subject: Post-call: scale responsiveness checklist & next steps
messages:
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Kapoor <samir.k@avaretail.com>, Ava Retail Ops <ops@avaretail.com>
Cc: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-06-15T15:12:00-07:00
Subject: Post-call: scale responsiveness checklist & next steps

Samir / Ava Ops team — thanks for the call earlier. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have a single source of truth. I added what we heard on SLOs and autoscale behavior and a short checklist for the PoC.

TL;DR from call:
- 95th pctl latency target (end-to-end, user-facing) = 150 ms for standard single-turn requests; streaming responses (multi-chunk assistant responses) need data chunks delivered every ~200ms once streaming starts.
- Expected steady-state throughput: 350–450 reqs/sec during peak promotions; sustained concurrency target = 60–80 active concurrent sessions.
- Critical for you: scale-up time and graceful queueing — you cannot accept >3s cold first-token delays at peak.

What we propose for the PoC:
1) Baseline perf run (traffic replay): Redwood will run a 30-min replay of a representative sample (you provide traces). Goal: verify 95th pctl and observe KV cache hit distribution.
2) Burst test: synthetic ramp to 2x peak for 10 min to validate warm pool and scale-up behavior.
3) Streaming verification: 5–10 long-response traces to confirm chunk cadence and partial token latency.
4) Failure modes: induce one host OOM to validate fallback to smaller model and queue handling (max queue length 120 before shedding).

Immediate asks from Ava:
- Share 1 hour of representative traffic trace (anonymized) and 10 sample long-response prompts (for streaming).
- Confirm which model family you want us to use for PoC (large-1024 vs medium-512) — impacts warm pool sizing and latency.

Next steps / owners:
- Samir: share traces and confirm model choice by Tue 6/17.
- Ava Ops: provide acceptance criteria for first-token threshold (is 3s acceptable as maximum for cold?)
- Redwood (Jonas): spin up PoC plan and share test harness endpoints + timelines by 6/18.

Attachments: latency_matrix_v1.xlsx (simple mapping of expected pctl targets), slo_checklist.md (checklist for PoC), warmpool-diagram.png (proposal for warm pool layout).

Thanks — I’m copying Evelyn to help with technical validation.

—Jonas

Jonas — thanks for the clear recap. A few clarifications from our side before we send traces: 

1) Model choice: prefer "large-1024" for quality during the PoC. We understand it will increase latency and memory; please indicate recommended warm pool sizing for that model.
2) For first-token SLA: our product owners say 3s max cold first-token is acceptable for non-critical admin flows, but customer-facing checkout flows need <800 ms first-token at p95. We'll flag which endpoints are critical in the traces.
3) Queueing: we cannot accept silent failures. If queue > threshold, we need a fast fallback to a concise summary response (smaller model) + 429/503 to clients where appropriate.

We will upload the anonymized traces and the list of long-response prompts to the shared Drive by EOD 6/16. Also attaching our internal severity matrix (uploaded separately) — it'll help prioritize which endpoints must stay sub-800ms.

Evelyn / Karthik — forwarding Samir's note and the details he confirmed. Key asks for engineering:

- Warm pool sizing recommendation for large-1024 and expected memory/slot counts. Samir expects to run checkout flows at sub-800ms p95; we need to propose warm pool + burst policy that guarantees that for the critical subset of traffic.
- Fallback behaviour: implement policy that routes to smaller model + returns a structured partial-response with a 429 code to clients when queue threshold crossed. Samir asked for no silent failures.
- Measurement: we'll need a short synthetic harness that can tag requests as "critical" vs "non-critical" to validate split SLAs. Could we produce a checklist and a rough time estimate for the PoC (spin-up time, test windows, required infra)?

I put the proposed test plan in slo_checklist.md attached in the thread. Can you review and add notes inline?

—Jonas

Thanks — flagged a few technical constraints and a recommended configuration below. Copying Samir so Ava can see the tradeoffs.

Quick notes: 
- Warm pool: for large-1024 we recommend an initial warm pool of 8 slots per region with a burst policy to add +12 slots (20 total) across 2 minutes. Warm instances keep KV cache primed; that reduces p95 significantly for identical prompts.
- Cold start: expected cold scale-up to first usable token ~3.5–4 minutes for a cold model boot on GPU (container + model load), so rely on warm pool for latency-sensitive flows.
- Warm pool scale-up time (adding warm slots): targeting 20–30s to reach new warm slot readiness (if using reserved instances), otherwise 90s–150s on shared capacity. Those numbers derive from kernel load + GUPIO provisioning.
- Queueing behavior: propose a two-level queueing policy:
  * Soft queue (per region) to buffer short spikes up to 120 requests; service ordering = FIFO, but critical-tagged requests are fast-tracked into top 20% of queue.
  * Hard threshold at 220 aggregated queued requests -> trigger shedding to smaller model and start returning 429 upward of that.
- Fallback model: medium-512 as concise-summary fallback; expected p95 for fallback ~250–350 ms but quality reduced.
- Streaming cadence: we can guarantee chunk emission interval <= 220ms for warmed sessions; cold sessions may see 350–500ms first few chunks until KV cache warms.

Action items: 
- Redwood (Evelyn + infra): I will prepare a short runbook and the exact CLI commands to create the warm pool and the burst policy. ETA: 6/19 morning.
- Ava: Samir to upload traces + critical endpoint list (due 6/16 — confirm upload complete).
- Redwood (Jonas): coordinate a 2-hour PoC window next week (ops + infra) once traces are in.

Attachments referenced in this thread: latency_matrix_v1.xlsx, slo_checklist.md, warmpool-diagram.png.
